haiku-low.q1: A message on the domain-events topic starts the consumer (DSP). The existing outbox relay produces that trigger.
haiku-low.q2: DSP matches active subscriptions by account_id and event_type, then inserts one delivery row per match in one transaction. A unique event_id plus subscription_id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a redelivered copy a no-op.
haiku-low.q3: The signature covers t + '.' + the stored body bytes, keyed by the decrypted subscription secret (HMAC-SHA256). It is regenerated with a fresh t on every attempt, including replays.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks done. 410 marks dead and disables the subscription. Other 4xx marks dead (client_error). Retryable failures (408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error) retry until the 8th failure, then dead.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the webhook service's own Postgres, not the core DB.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as a pending row with next_attempt_at set. A sender's 1-second poll claims it once due, so no queue delay is used.
haiku-low.q8: The row stays in sending until lease_until (claim time plus 60 s) expires. The next worker to poll re-claims it. The lost try still counts toward the 8, and the receiver may see it twice.
haiku-low.q9: Dead rows stay in the deliveries table with status dead, not a separate queue. Replay sets it back to pending, attempt_count 0, next_attempt_at now, same id. Replay into a disabled subscription gets 409.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header, which stays the same across attempts and replays. Receivers use it for dedupe.
haiku-low.q11: When a sender claims such a delivery, it is marked dead with reason subscription_disabled and no HTTP request is sent.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. The document states there is no ordering between events, and retries reorder things.

sonnet.q1: Domain events on the domain-events topic, fed by the existing outbox relay, are consumed by the DSP consumer.
sonnet.q2: DSP matches active subscriptions (same account_id, event_type in list or '*') and inserts one DLV row per match in one transaction, committing before ack. A unique key on event_id + subscription_id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a redelivered copy's re-insert a no-op.
sonnet.q3: HMAC-SHA256, keyed with the subscription's decrypted secret, over t + '.' + the stored body bytes (sent as X-Webhook-Signature t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>). It is redone with a fresh t on every attempt, replays included.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: done (delivered). 410: marked dead (reason gone) and the subscription is disabled (disabled_reason gone). Other 4xx: dead (client_error). Retryable failures (408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error): back to pending with a delay, or dead (retries_exhausted) if it was the 8th attempt.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails (next_attempt_at = now + 2m).
sonnet.q6: In the deliveries table (DLV store) in the webhook service's own Postgres: status, attempt_count, next_attempt_at, lease_until, last_status_code, last_error, dead_reason, dead_at, plus the body bytes.
sonnet.q7: It waits as a pending row in the deliveries table with next_attempt_at set. A sender's 1s poll claims it once it is due. No queue delays are used.
sonnet.q8: The row stays in `sending` until lease_until (claim time + 60 s) expires. Then whichever worker polls next re-claims it and retries. The lost try still counts toward the 8, and the receiver may see the request twice (at-least-once). A late original sender can write its outcome only if attempt_count still equals what it claimed.
sonnet.q9: They are held in the same deliveries table as job rows with status=dead (the 'DLQ' is not a separate queue). Replay flips the record back to pending with attempt_count reset to 0 and next_attempt_at = now, under the same id.
sonnet.q10: The delivery id, sent as X-Webhook-Id. It never changes across attempts or replays.
sonnet.q11: When a sender claims such a delivery and finds the subscription disabled, it marks it dead with reason subscription_disabled and makes no HTTP call. It then sits in the DLQ.
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering between events, and retries reorder things.
